audits.title: EP-250 A closed-loop clinical audit on the impact of implementing the STAR Score at a tertiary level hospital in India: Where do we stand?
audits.standard: STAR (Surgical Tool for Auditing Records) and standard guidelines
audits.setting: All surgical departments, MGM Medical College & Hospital, tertiary hospital

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 74%; general surgery and orthopaedics 82% each, neurosurgery lowest at 62%. Most missing information was anaesthetic records and subsequent entries.

audits.intervention: Series of departmental training and implementation meetings.

cycle2.result: Compliance improved to 90% in all departments.

audits.other_findings: Anaesthetic records were the most frequently missing items at baseline.
audits.citation: Sinha A, Kadam S. EP-250 A closed-loop clinical audit on the impact of implementing the STAR Score at a tertiary level hospital in India: Where do we stand?. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_5). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac245.065.

audits.title: EP-271 Assessing the Impact of Implementing the STAR Score at a Tertiary Level Hospital in India: A Closed-loop Clinical Audit
audits.standard: STAR (Surgical Tool for Auditing Records) standards
audits.setting: General surgery department, MGM Medical College & Hospital (tertiary hospital)

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 82%; consent 7% and anaesthetic records 14% lowest.

audits.intervention: Series of departmental training sessions and meetings.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 95%; all sections significantly improved; consent and anaesthetic records increased by 75% and 70%.

audits.citation: Sinha A, Kadam S. EP-271 Assessing the Impact of Implementing the STAR Score at a Tertiary Level Hospital in India: A Closed-loop Clinical Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_5). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac245.071.

audits.title: FP5.12 - Write what you know: A retrospective documentation audit
audits.standard: Royal College of Physicians: every entry dated, timed and signed with name and designation, standardised structure and chronological order
audits.setting: General, colorectal and vascular surgery inpatients, district general hospital (Princess Alexandra Hospital)

cycle1.result: 89.8% dated; 42.0% timed; 93.2% standardised structure; 6.8% had author designation and 3.4% signature.

audits.other_findings: Admission entries had the most consistent structure; suggested causes include inadequate junior doctor training, ward round pace and reliance on electronic notes.
audits.citation: Ibanga U, Lingam G, Sivarajah V. FP5.12 - Write what you know: A retrospective documentation audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae197.389.

audits.title: A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit of Surgical Documentation of Inpatient Records at a Tertiary Level Hospital in Egypt.
audits.standard: Hospital protocol with STAR and CRABEL audit tools
audits.setting: Surgical oncology department, Alexandria Main University Hospital

cycle1.result: Anaesthetic record 90.65±4.3; operative record 86.15±5.347; discharge summary 96±0.0.

audits.intervention: Preprepared templates, staff education and systematic auditing.

cycle2.result: Anaesthetic record 100±0.0; operative record 95.6±3.365; all domains improved except discharge summary.

audits.citation: Hassan AG, Elqaffas EO, Elbouridy AM, Shawky MM, El-Fayoumi TA. A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit of Surgical Documentation of Inpatient Records at a Tertiary Level Hospital in Egypt. Cureus. 2023;15(12):e49862. doi:10.7759/cureus.49862. PMID: 38170126.

audits.title: Current trends on clinical audit on surgical record keeping.
audits.standard: Local trust record-keeping policy: 30 standards, 10 with 100% target and 20 with 75% target
audits.setting: Surgical department, Whiston Hospital, Mersey and West Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Significant deficits including illegible entries, missing clinician designations and inconsistent use of approved abbreviations.

cycle2.result: Improvements in some areas such as documentation of date and time; further effort needed across all standards.

audits.other_findings: Recommendations: improved induction training, standardised documentation layouts and prompt recording.
audits.citation: Singla L. Current trends on clinical audit on surgical record keeping. Bioinformation. 2024;20(11):1654-1657. doi:10.6026/9732063002001654. PMID: 40162469.

audits.title: Enhancing the Quality of Surgical Documentation Through the Surgical Tool for Auditing Records (STAR): Experience From a Tertiary Care Hospital in South Asia.
audits.standard: Surgical Tool for Auditing Records (STAR), 50 criteria in six domains

cycle2.result: Mean STAR score 77.11 ± 7.17 (p < 0.001); discharge summary 94.44 ± 5.61; diagnosis recorded in 50% (24/48).

audits.other_findings: Consent remained the lowest-scoring domain; consent and anaesthetic records did not improve significantly.
audits.citation: Abdul Mubarack OMO, Wickramasinghe D, Wickramasinghe DP.
